tools.name: duckdb_data_query
tools.desc: Query data with DuckDB SQL and get the rows back as JSON (or CSV, or a Markdown table): files and globs (CSV, JSON, Parquet, Excel), URLs, S3 and Azure paths, the previous flow step's output (the table input), and databases attached read-only (Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle, DuckDB files). Reads, joins, filters, transforms and aggregates in one query; save_to also writes the result to a CSV, JSON or Parquet file.

params.name: sql
params.desc: The DuckDB SQL. Several statements run in turn; the last one's rows are the result. Tables: the sources' names, input, and connection.schema.table
params.example: SELECT region, sum(total) AS revenue FROM orders GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC

params.name: sources
params.desc: Files, globs, URLs or s3:// paths to query, as tables: {"name": "location"}

params.name: connections
params.desc: Databases to attach (read-only unless "read_only": false): [{"name", "type": postgres | mysql | sqlite | sqlserver | oracle | duckdb, "dsn"}]. ${NAME} in a dsn is filled from a secret or environment variable (PGPASSWORD and MYSQL_PWD are read by the drivers themselves).

params.name: extensions
params.desc: DuckDB extensions to load as well, comma-separated (those the sources and connections need load by themselves); community ones as name@community

params.name: input
params.desc: A file with the previous step's output (in a flow: {{input_file}}), queried as the table input

params.name: save_to
params.desc: Also write the whole result to this file: .csv, .json or .parquet

params.name: max_rows
params.desc: At most this many rows in the answer (save_to writes all of them)

secrets.name: PGPASSWORD
secrets.desc: Postgres password (read by the Postgres driver)

secrets.name: MYSQL_PWD
secrets.desc: MySQL password (read by the MySQL driver)

secrets.name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
secrets.desc: AWS access key for S3 (otherwise your AWS profile or SSO is used)

secrets.name: AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
secrets.desc: AWS session token for S3 (temporary credentials)

secrets.name: ORACLE_PASSWORD
secrets.desc: Oracle password, used as ${ORACLE_PASSWORD} in a dsn

secrets.name: MSSQL_PASSWORD
secrets.desc: SQL Server password, used as ${MSSQL_PASSWORD} in a dsn
